items.headline: Bessent unveils 'Operation Economic Outcast': ~60 entities sanctioned, China warned but not yet directly targeted
items.summary: Treasury's Monday 2pm ET rollout designated roughly 60 entities, vessels and individuals across UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland for enabling Iran's oil-revenue network, and announced five new secondary-sanctions categories (digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, shipping) that will be phased in via country-by-country deadlines rather than imposed immediately. Asked if Chinese banks could be hit, Bessent said 'no one is above the reach of U.S. sanctions' without naming China directly. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei repeated a threat to halt Hormuz flow if Gulf states join the crackdown, but no closure or shipping incident has been confirmed.
items.actionable: The threat to China was rhetorical, not executed -- a genuine escalation would be a Chinese-bank secondary-sanction headline, which would be the sharper risk-off jolt for the HK tech sleeve (0700.HK/0981.HK/1810.HK); until then this reads as contained rather than a fresh shock.

items.headline: Oil sells off on the sanctions 'sell the news' -- WTI/Brent both -2.5% Monday after a two-week rally priced the rollout in
items.summary: WTI fell to $84.89 and Brent to $92.06 (both -2.5%) as traders took profits after the pair rallied 5.6-6.4% over the prior week anticipating Monday's announcement. Commodity-vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz reportedly stayed thin (fewer than 20 over the weekend) amid the ongoing Iran/US friction, a structural condition rather than a new Monday development.
items.actionable: Don't read the pullback as the sanctions story fading -- a stalled Hormuz chokepoint is a slow-burn bullish setup for gold/silver as a geopolitical hedge even while oil itself chops on positioning.

items.headline: Gold hits a 3-month high (~$4,649-4,681/oz) as the Treasury-buyback dollar slide keeps extending
items.summary: Spot gold rose roughly 1% Monday to its highest since mid-May, futures +0.6% to $4,706.20, as markets awaited this week's inflation data and Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole debut. GLD itself closed +0.79% at $426.69. Silver extended the same breakout, trading $69-70/oz intraday (SLV closed -0.83% at $62.20, a modest pause within the up-trend), a move press is framing as +18% month-over-month and one of the sharpest of 2026 -- both driven by the same Treasury-buyback/dollar-debasement dynamic rather than an Iran-specific bid.
items.actionable: The breakout is intact into Wednesday's Nvidia print and Friday's Jackson Hole -- no reason to de-risk the miners sleeve pre-open unless Warsh surprises hawkish.

items.headline: KOSPI falls 3.1% Monday on chip-stock selloff and yield pressure; foreign/institutional selling absorbed by retail
items.summary: Korean press report KOSPI closed around 6,696.96 (-3.12%) Monday as Samsung Electronics fell over 4-8.7% and SK Hynix also declined, amid broader Asia weakness tied to bond-market yield pressure and the same pre-Nvidia-earnings chip jitters hitting US semis. Foreigners net sold roughly W3.7-3.9tn and institutions ~W1.3-1.7tn (Korean-press sources disagree on the exact figure), while individuals net bought ~W3.3-3.8tn, absorbing the selling almost entirely -- a similar 'retail buys the dip' pattern to the prior week's round trip. Hang Seng also fell (~1.9% per AP-syndicated coverage), consistent with Tencent's -3.72% Monday move already on the tape.
items.actionable: A genuine leg down in North Asia tech ahead of Wednesday's Nvidia print -- worth watching whether Tuesday's HK/SG open extends the move or the KOSPI pattern of institutional buy-the-dip repeats.

items.headline: Hong Kong Southbound flips back to a HK$11.6bn net buy Monday after Friday's HK$7.6bn outflow -- mainland money bought Tencent, sold SMIC
items.summary: Mainland investors bought a net HK$11.57bn of HK stocks via Southbound Stock Connect on Monday 24 Aug (Alibaba +HK$2.18bn, Tencent +HK$1.54bn), reversing Friday 21 Aug's HK$7.63bn net outflow. SMIC was sold (-HK$1.90bn) even as the broader flow turned positive -- a stock-specific divergence within the owner's HK tech book.
items.actionable: Mainland conviction stayed selectively constructive on Tencent specifically even as SMIC was sold and the KOSPI-led chip selloff weighed on the sector -- consistent with a stock-picking, not a broad de-risking, mainland stance.

items.headline: Xiaomi unveils three self-developed chips including a flagship 3nm smartphone processor
items.summary: Xiaomi announced in-house smartphone, AI and self-driving processors -- its most aggressive semiconductor self-sufficiency push yet -- though analysts flag high costs and limited manufacturing scale before these reach volume production.
items.actionable: A genuine long-term vertical-integration catalyst for Xiaomi; watch whether SMIC is named as the fab partner, which would be the direct read-through trade for 0981.HK.

items.headline: US-Canada trade talks collapse; Trump imposes 50% tariffs on ~$20bn of Canadian goods, Canada vows to match dollar-for-dollar
items.summary: Talks broke down Friday 21 Aug; the US then imposed 50% tariffs on a swath of Canadian goods (hockey sticks, building materials, liquor, some apparel) worth roughly $20bn. PM Carney said Canada would match the tariffs dollar-for-dollar; USTR Greer blamed Canada for 'wanting more.' Actively cited Monday as part of the mixed-close macro backdrop alongside the chip selloff.
items.actionable: A second live trade-friction front alongside the Iran sanctions -- adds to the case for staying patient on the large cash pile rather than chasing Friday's rebound, though it has no direct read-through to the book's specific holdings.

items.headline: Bitcoin nears $80k on the same Treasury-buyback dollar weakness lifting gold, plus Clarity Act momentum
items.summary: BTC traded $78,000-79,140 Monday, roughly +22% on the week and its highest since May, on continued short-covering, Trump's public backing of the Clarity Act, and efforts to bring crypto derivatives platform Hyperliquid onshore -- the same debasement narrative driving gold/silver rather than an independent catalyst.
items.actionable: $80k is the next technical level into Jackson Hole; a clean break would likely coincide with, not diverge from, further gold/silver strength given the shared driver -- treat BTC as a levered extension of the metals trade, not a diversifier.

items.headline: Jackson Hole: Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair set for Friday -- markets split on tone, the week's biggest single event risk
items.summary: Warsh has deliberately pulled back from Powell-style forward guidance, telling reporters his remarks will focus on 'long-term structural questions,' not near-term policy signals. A BofA fund-manager survey shows 69% expecting a neutral tone, while futures price roughly 1-in-3 odds of a September hike.
items.actionable: Bigger event risk for the metals trade than Wednesday's Nvidia print -- Friday's tone is the swing factor for whether the gold/silver breakout extends or reverses; avoid adding fresh leverage into it.

items.headline: Japan Core CPI due 13:00 SGT today -- July's 1.9% print (highest this year) already strengthens BOJ September-hike bets
items.summary: Japan's headline inflation hit 1.9% in July, energy-driven partly by the Iran-war oil spike; several APAC economists say the trend reinforces conviction the BOJ's next move is a September hike. Today's release is the next data point testing that call.
items.actionable: A hot print reinforcing BOJ-hike bets could strengthen the yen and pressure regional risk appetite right at the HKEX/SGX open -- a pre-market flag to watch rather than a trade signal until the number lands.

items.headline: Nvidia's FQ2 earnings (Wed 26 Aug after close) now one trading day away -- the week's cleanest AI-capex read, after Monday's chip stocks sold off into it
items.summary: Micron, AMD, TSM and Nvidia itself all fell Monday (roughly -1.3% to -5.8%) as AI-capex-fatigue positioning built ahead of Wednesday's print, the cleanest single test of whether the mid-August capex-durability scare was overdone or real.
items.actionable: The book has no direct Nvidia exposure but XLK/SMH/QQQ-adjacent sentiment sets the tone for HK tech and the broader risk-on/off read into Thursday's Asia open -- a binary, dated catalyst worth watching rather than trading around blind.
